EXAMS: US BREAST BIOPSY, MA 3D DIGITAL DIAGNOSTIC MAMMOGRAPHY (LEFT BREAST)

HISTORY: 71 years old female with left 10:00, 2 cm from nipple, ill-defined sonographic mass, which
corresponds to a left upper central mammographic mass on recent diagnostic evaluation. The patient
presents for ultrasound guided core biopsy.

PROCEDURE: Ultrasound guided core biopsy of the left breast.

Pertinent imaging studies and/or documents were reviewed prior to the procedure. The patient
identification and procedure were verified. The patient's known allergies, current medications and
adverse medication reactions were reviewed prior to the procedure. The procedure was explained to
the patient [REDACTED] infection and
bleeding, were reviewed. Patient's questions were answered and written informed consent was
obtained.

A safety pause was performed immediately prior to the procedure.

PRE PROCEDURE IMAGING: Re-demonstrates the lesion described above.

The patient [REDACTED] obtained. The breast was prepped for the
procedure using standard aseptic technique. Local anesthesia was achieved with injection of 7 cc of
1% lidocaine in the skin/superficial tissues and the deeper tissues. The mass was biopsied using a
lateral approach, ultrasound guidance and a 14 gauge spring loaded core biopsy needle device. 5
tissue samples were obtained. Adequate lesion sampling was confirmed by orthogonal ultrasound
images. The tissue specimens were placed in formalin and submitted to the pathologist [REDACTED]
analysis.

A ribbon tissue marker was then deployed at the biopsy site.

Digital post biopsy CC and MLO mammographic views were performed. The breast tissue is
heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. Left central inner breast, posterior depth,

IMPRESSION:

Left ultrasound guided core biopsy of the sonographic mass at 10:00, 2 cm from the nipple complete.
Ribbon biopsy marker was placed.

Postbiopsy mammogram demonstrates the ribbon clip in the left central inner breast, corresponding to
the irregular mammographic mass. Slightly superior, approximately 0.9 cm superiorly, to the ribbon
clip on MLO view there is a second mammographic asymmetry, which appears relatively stable compared
to prior exams. Given close proximity, this will likely be included in the treatment field.

PATHOLOGY RESULTS:

Invasive ductal carcinoma. Please refer to pathology report for complete results.

Pathology shows malignant findings. The results are concordant with imaging.

RECOMMENDATION:

1.Recommendation: Surgical consultation. Surgery consultation/excision and appropriate medical
management is recommended for the left 10:00 (ribbon clip) biopsy-proven invasive ductal carcinoma.

2. Pre and postcontrast breast MRI can be considered to evaluate for extent of disease.
